newsitem.title: USA: Elsag Bailey tumbles, bookings cited.
newsitem.headline: Elsag Bailey tumbles, bookings cited.

text.p: Elsag Bailey Process Automations NV shares fell 28 percent on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday morning after a delayed opening as analysts downgraded the stock amid concerns over bookings.
Merrill Lynch cut its near-term rating on the stock by two notches, to neutral from buy, but retained its long-term buy rating.
Alex Brown downgraded the stock to neutral from buy, while McDonald & Co went to hold from buy on the Netherlands-based maker of equipment and systems for industrial process control.
McDonald analyst Michael Linsky said the company's third-quarter earnings of $0.55 a share exceeded his estimate by one penny.

"The rating downgrade principally reflects the adverse EPS implications for the fourth quarter and 1997 of 1) softer third-quarter bookings -- basically with respect to large systems business -- than we had been envisioning, despite recently reduced bookings expectations, and 2) the evident likelihood that fourth-quarter orders will not be as strong as we earlier had thought probable," he said.
Linsky cut his earnings estimate on Elsag to $0.63 a share from $0.94 for the fourth quarter, and to $2.00 from $2.35 for 1997.
